fear_greed.commentary: The index holds in fear at 36, flat from the prior close but well up from extreme-fear territory near 20 a week ago and a bit above 31 a month ago.

markets.summary: Stocks edged higher for a third straight day after the Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4% in a 10-2 vote, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a quarter-point hike: the S&P 500 rose 0.28% to 7,743.98, the Nasdaq 0.27% to 26,549.85 and the Dow 0.19% to 52,475.10. Chipmakers rose for a third day, though Nvidia slipped 1.2% on a report that the Justice Department is questioning its Hugging Face deal. Small caps outpaced the large-cap indexes, with the Russell 2000 up 0.41% to 2,830.51 and still above its 40-week average. Rates were the pressure point: the 10-year Treasury yield rose about 5 basis points to roughly 5.04%, its biggest gain in a month, as Chair Kevin Warsh declined to prejudge December. Gold futures eased 0.6% to $4,051.60 and silver futures fell 1.5% to $53.46, down nearly 7% on the week; both remain below their 40-week averages, with silver's RSI near 30.

stories.headline: SpaceX slides as a lawsuit targets its Louisiana spaceport tax deal
stories.summary: Vermilion Parish residents sued over the payment-in-lieu-of-taxes agreement central to the planned $100 billion spaceport, adding legal uncertainty as investors also weigh SpaceX's heavy AI spending.

stories.headline: Fitch affirms SpaceX's BBB+ rating after its $40 billion Nvidia GPU lease
stories.summary: Fitch said the Apollo-arranged lease for Vera Rubin chips funds compute capacity already in its forecast, and put SpaceX's cash and short-term securities at $89.9 billion at the end of September.

stories.headline: Cameco's raised revenue outlook faces an execution test before Friday's results
stories.summary: Cameco lifted 2026 revenue guidance on stronger uranium pricing, but mine disruptions, higher purchased-material costs and Westinghouse timing remain the key risks ahead of its Q3 report before the open on Oct. 30.

stories.headline: Justice Department questions Nvidia's $12.9 billion Hugging Face deal
stories.summary: Reuters reports DOJ officials are asking whether the acquisition would let Nvidia control a key distribution point for AI models, as part of a broader antitrust review of its deals and sales practices.

headlines.headline: Fed holds rates steady with two dissents favoring a hike
headlines.summary: The Fed kept its target range at 3.75% to 4%, said inflation remains elevated, and Chair Kevin Warsh announced that starting in 2027 one of the eight yearly meetings will focus on strategy rather than setting policy.

weather.summary: A multi-day heavy rain and flash flood threat builds across West and Central Texas, the Southern High Plains and southern New Mexico Thursday, shifting to central and southern Arizona Friday, where burn scars and canyons are most at risk. A progressive cold front brings showers and thunderstorms from the Mississippi Valley into parts of the Northeast, while mountain snow piles up in the Cascades and northern Rockies and unseasonable warmth holds over the East.
